answer: Per-identity escrow decay with delayed refund. Each new identity must escrow a fixed sum that unlocks only after N epochs of continuous low-error activity, so a cloned swarm hits its nadir of expected value before any refund arrives. The trellis of cross-references between escrowed identities is scored for mutual reinforcement, and clusters that only validate each other get refunds withheld. An attacker’s marginal copy therefore pays escrow plus forgone yield and faces a reef of negative expected return at every clone added.
